data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following a checklist is significantly more reliable than a single expert because the checklist converts a 'stochastic' intuitive process into a 'deterministic' algorithmic process, eliminating the expert's primary failure mode: cognitive variability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires 'abductive leaps' or synthesis that cannot be decomposed into a finite set of checklist items.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist itself contains a systemic error that the non-experts lack the domain knowledge to identify.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of the 'ceiling of mediocrity' (missing the 1% of complex cases only an expert sees) outweighs the benefit of eliminating the 10% of simple errors.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Algorithmic Floor' effect: While an expert's intuition allows for higher peak performance, it suffers from high variance due to mood, fatigue, or subconscious bias. A checklist imposes a minimum standard of execution (a floor) that prevents the catastrophic 'silly mistakes' that plague experts, while the panel's collective verification ensures the algorithm is executed without omission.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
